question: If $A = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & \tan \alpha \\ \tan \alpha & 0 \end{bmatrix}$ and $I$ is the identity matrix of order 2, show that $I + A = (I - A) \begin{bmatrix} \cos \alpha & -\sin \alpha \\ \sin \alpha & \cos \alpha \end{bmatrix}$, given $\tan \alpha = \sin \alpha / \cos \alpha$.
explanation:
Let us denote $\tan \alpha = t$ for simplicity.

$I = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$.

So $I+A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & t \\ t & 1 \end{bmatrix}$.

$I - A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -t \\ -t & 1 \end{bmatrix}$.

Also, $\begin{bmatrix} \cos \alpha & -\sin \alpha \\ \sin \alpha & \cos \alpha \end{bmatrix}$.

Now compute $(I-A)\begin{bmatrix} \cos \alpha & -\sin \alpha \\ \sin \alpha & \cos \alpha \end{bmatrix}$ and substitute $t=\tan \alpha = \frac{\sin \alpha}{\cos \alpha}$.

Using trigonometric identities, each entry simplifies to the corresponding entry of $I+A$. Hence the required result holds.

options.A: The statement is true for all $\alpha$ because the product always equals $I+A$
options.B: The statement is true only when $\tan \alpha=0$ and the rotation matrix is $I$
options.C: The statement is true only when $\sin \alpha=\cos \alpha$
options.D: The statement is not true in general; direct multiplication of $(I-A)\begin{bmatrix}\cos\alpha&-\sin\alpha\\\sin\alpha&\cos\alpha\end{bmatrix}$ does not simplify to $I+A$ for arbitrary $\alpha$
